primary_claim: The author develops an algorithm to generate synthetic datasets from a high-dimensional percolation-theory data model, with associated ground-truth hierarchical latent features, intended as a testbed for validating interpretability tools
stated_future_work: Scale up the synthetic datasets, train neural networks on the data, and interpret those networks
Develop interpretability metrics for these datasets that trade off breadth and depth of recovered concepts
Investigate whether similar failure modes (e.g. feature splitting) occur across synthetic and natural data distributions to test the percolation model's predictive power
Present derivations of create_prob and split_prob parameter values, and full algorithm details, in a forthcoming publication
limitations_stated: Data generation and embedding procedures are stochastic, so studies should be repeated using multiple datasets generated with different random seeds
Embedding procedure relies on approximate orthogonality of random vectors in high dimensions; embedding dimension of O(100) or greater recommended to avoid discrepancies
A generated dataset represents a full data distribution; only a tiny subset should be used for training to obtain a realistic ML dataset analog
quote: It employs a newly developed algorithm to construct a dataset in a way that explicitly and iteratively reveals its innate hierarchical structure.
